title: Deploying ML Models
subtitle: Saving models, building APIs, and serving predictions

content.text: Persist a trained model with joblib or pickle and serve it via a REST API for real-time predictions.

content.code:
import joblib
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel
import numpy as np

# Save model
joblib.dump(model, "model.joblib")
joblib.dump(scaler, "scaler.joblib")

# Load and serve
model = joblib.load("model.joblib")
scaler = joblib.load("scaler.joblib")

app = FastAPI()

class Features(BaseModel):
    age: float
    income: float

@app.post("/predict")
def predict(f: Features):
    X = np.array([[f.age, f.income]])
    X_scaled = scaler.transform(X)
    pred = model.predict(X_scaled)[0]
    prob = model.predict_proba(X_scaled)[0, 1]
    return {"prediction": int(pred), "probability": float(prob)}

content.text: Always save the scaler alongside the model — predictions on unscaled data will be wrong.

questions.question: Why must you save the scaler with the model?
options: Because predictions need the same transformation applied during training
questions.explanation: Predictions must pass through the same scaling used during training, or the inputs will be on a different scale.

faq.a: When model performance degrades over time because real-world data distributions change. Monitor predictions vs actual outcomes in production.
